extra.message: The 404 error handler passes attacker-controlled request.path into render_template_string() inside an f-string. Jinja2 evaluates the resulting template, so a request to a URL containing template syntax (e.g. /{{7*7}} or {{config}}/{{ malicious }}) results in Server-Side Template Injection, which can lead to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Flask app.secret_key is hardcoded to the predictable value 'super secret key'. This key signs session cookies; with a known secret an attacker can forge arbitrary session cookies (including authenticating as any user / admin) using flask-unsign or itsdangerous.

User-supplied request.args.get('search') is interpolated via an f-string directly into a SQLAlchemy text() clause: text(f"text like '%{search_param}%'"). The value is not parameterized, allowing SQL injection (e.g. a search value that closes the quote and appends UNION/OR conditions) against the notes query.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The registration code (form.registration_code.data) is interpolated via an f-string directly into a raw SQL query executed with session.execute(text(...)): "SELECT id, code FROM ... WHERE code = '{code}'". The unparameterized input allows SQL injection, enabling authentication-code bypass or data exfiltration during signup.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The before_request handler reads the attacker-controlled 'preferences' cookie and passes it to pickle.loads(b64decode(...)). Deserializing untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary code execution: an attacker can craft a malicious base64-encoded pickle cookie whose __reduce__ executes arbitrary commands on the server.

urlopen(url) is called with a user-controlled URL passed from the /account/image route (form.url.data -> get_base64_image_blob -> download). There is no validation of scheme or host, allowing Server-Side Request Forgery: attackers can make the server fetch internal services (http://169.254.169.254/, localhost), or use file:// to read local files, returning the content base64-encoded in the profile image.

The update_account POST handler lacks the @login_required decorator (unlike the GET /account). It updates current_user attributes from the submitted form. Combined with mass assignment (current_user.__dict__.update(filtered_values)) and the AccountForm exposing an is_admin BooleanField, a user can submit is_admin=true to escalate themselves to administrator. This is broken access control / privilege escalation.

current_user.__dict__.update(filtered_values) blindly applies all submitted form fields to the user model. Because AccountForm includes an is_admin BooleanField, an attacker can set is_admin=true in the POST body to elevate their account to administrator (mass assignment / privilege escalation).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: get_personal_notes(user_id) queries all notes filtered only by the user_id taken directly from the URL path, with no check that the requested user_id matches current_user.id. Any authenticated user can read any other user's notes — including private notes — by changing the user_id in /accounts/<user_id>/notes. This is an Insecure Direct Object Reference / broken access control.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: delete_note(note_id) fetches and deletes a note by the id from the URL without verifying that note.user_id equals current_user.id. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's note by supplying an arbitrary note_id, an Insecure Direct Object Reference / missing ownership authorization check.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Note text, which is user-supplied and stored unsanitized (forms/note_form.py applies no sanitization), is rendered with the Jinja2 | safe filter ({{ note.text | safe }}), disabling autoescaping. This results in stored Cross-Site Scripting: a malicious note containing <script> executes in the browser of every user who views the home page (notes are shared when not private).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: render_table is called with safe_columns=['text'], which marks the user-controlled note text column as safe/unescaped. Stored, unsanitized note text is rendered as raw HTML, enabling stored Cross-Site Scripting on the search results page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: render_table is called with safe_columns=['text'], rendering the user-controlled, unsanitized note text column as raw HTML on the personal notes page. This enables stored Cross-Site Scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /darkmode POST handler has no @login_required decorator and writes a pickled 'preferences' cookie via pickle.dumps. Lacking authentication control and combined with the pickle deserialization in before_request, this endpoint contributes to the insecure-deserialization attack surface and access-control weakness.

The SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, causing all SQL statements (including those containing sensitive data such as password hashes, emails and registration codes) to be logged to stdout/stderr. This is a sensitive data exposure / security misconfiguration in a production setting.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: A static, hardcoded registration code 'a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764' is seeded into the database. Anyone who knows this value (it is in source control) can register a new account, bypassing the intended invitation-only registration control.
